docs.text: SpPy ¶ SpPy provides one- and two-dimensional sparse arrays backed by Eigen's C++ sparse matrix library. It stores entries and their coordinates instead of a value for every position, making arrays with many zeros more economical. Use it for sparse vectors and matrices, slicing, arithmetic, reductions, and linear algebra with a NumPy-style interface. import numpy as np import sppy a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]]) product = a @ a # Matrix multiplication squared = a * a # Elementwise multiplication column_sums = a.sum(axis=0) # Dense result: [3., 2.] dense = np.asarray(a) # Explicitly allocate a dense array Start with installation and the quick start , then explore the sparse array guide . Existing users should read the 1.0 migration guide . What to expect ¶ Signed integer storage: int8 , int16 , int32 , and int64 . Floating-point storage: float32 and float64 ; complex: complex64 and complex128 . Row-major ( order="C" ) and column-major ( order="F" ) matrices. Optional SciPy conversion and Matrix Market IO . Linear solvers, Frobenius norms, and randomized SVD . SpPy requires Python 3.11+, NumPy 2, Eigen 5.0.1+, and a C++17 compiler to build. It supports vectors and matrices, rather than arbitrary-dimensional tensors. Unsigned and boolean storage are unsupported. NumPy compatibility is partial; see interoperability and limits . See Eigen coverage for supported modules and boundaries. Project and support ¶ Report bugs and request features in the GitHub issue tracker . For build problems, include your operating system, Python/compiler versions, Eigen location, command, and full error output. See contributing for validation and documentation commands.

Contributing ¶ Set up the development environment before running package checks. Build and preview the documentation ¶ The documentation uses MkDocs and mkdocstrings. API pages are extracted from Python source without importing native extensions, so documentation-only work does not require Eigen, a compiler, or an installed SpPy package. uv sync --locked --only-group docs uv run --locked --only-group docs mkdocs serve Open the local address printed by MkDocs (normally http://127.0.0.1:8000 ). The preview reloads when documentation changes. To build the static site: uv run --locked --only-group docs mkdocs build --strict Output is written to site/ . Strict builds fail on warnings, including broken page links and anchors, and run in CI. Navigation lives in mkdocs.yml ; content lives in docs/*.md . API reference directives read the public Python source. Use relative Markdown links between pages and runnable Python code blocks. --only-group docs installs only documentation dependencies. Run uv sync --locked again before working on native code or running tests. To keep both environments installed, use uv sync --locked --group docs and uv run --locked --group docs mkdocs serve with Eigen configured. Checks and release builds ¶ With the default development environment: uv run --locked pytest uv run --locked ruff check . uv run --locked ruff format --check sppy tests profiling uv run --locked clang-format --dry-run --Werror sppy/native/*.h sppy/native/*.cpp uv build uv build writes the source distribution and wheel to dist/ . Native bindings are compiled from sppy/native/ using pybind11 and Eigen. setup.py and MANIFEST.in are no longer needed; package and archive settings live in pyproject.toml . After editing dependency declarations, run uv lock and commit the lockfile. After changing external Eigen headers, force a rebuild: uv sync --locked --reinstall-package sppy For optional OpenMP: export SPPY_OPENMP=1 uv sync --locked --reinstall-package sppy uv run --locked pytest uv build The compiler and linker must support OpenMP and its runtime must be available. Keep SPPY_OPENMP set for subsequent commands. Alternatively, release builds accept uv build -Ccmake.define.SPPY_OPENMP=ON . Without OpenMP, parallel kernels run serially. Tests and profiling layout ¶ The pytest suite lives in the repository's top-level tests/ directory. Tests use Arrange–Act–Assert sections, parametrized cases, isolated temporary files, and local random generators. Run a focused subset with, for example, uv run pytest tests/test_numpy_compatibility.py . Tests of the actual native extension boundary run with uv run pytest -m native ; no second compiler invocation is needed. Numerical solver and storage contracts are in tests/test_eigen_features.py . sppy.test() locates checkout tests and does not search installed packages. Runtime wheels do not include tests or profiling tools; source archives do. Opt-in profiling tools are in profiling/ . For example: uv run --locked python -m profiling.benchmark --operations all --size 1000 --output /tmp/sppy-benchmark.json uv run --locked python -m profiling.profile --operation matmat --backend sppy_C --output /tmp/sppy.prof See the profiling guide for workload settings, profile files, and benchmark output. Importing these modules performs no profiling or input generation. The native build directory is reused to speed incremental builds. To switch an existing OpenMP build off, explicitly rebuild with SPPY_OPENMP=0 . Do not mutate a sparse array concurrently with a native operation on that same array. Reusable direct factorization methods serialize access to their state.

docs.text: Arrays and constructors ¶ For examples and storage behavior, see the sparse array guide . SparseArray is the public array class. Legacy aliases have been removed. Constructors ¶ sppy.util ¶ Factories for owned Eigen sparse arrays. asarray(a, dtype=None, order=None, *, copy=None) ¶ Convert data to sparse storage, reusing compatible sparse input if possible. zeros(shape, dtype=float, *, order='C') ¶ Create an empty sparse vector or matrix. ones(shape, dtype=float, *, order='C') ¶ Create an array storing one at every position. eye(n, m=None, k=0, dtype=float, order='C') ¶ Create a sparse identity, optionally rectangular or offset by k. diag(v, k=0, *, order='C') ¶ Construct an offset diagonal or extract one from a matrix. rand(shape, density, dtype=float, *, order='C', rng=None) ¶ Sample values at random coordinates, with replacement. Pass a NumPy Generator for reproducible input. Actual density can be lower than requested because duplicate coordinates overwrite earlier samples. SparseArray ¶ The constructor accepts a shape or existing data. A tuple is interpreted as a shape; use sppy.asarray to treat a tuple as values. The constructor defaults to row storage; order="C" or order="F" explicitly selects storage. Properties include shape , ndim , size , dtype , order , nnz , and T . nnz counts stored entries; use count_nonzero for nonzero values. parallel_dot uses Eigen kernels; OpenMP builds can run supported kernels in parallel. Without OpenMP, the kernels run serially. sppy.sparse_array.SparseArray(data, dtype=None, *, order='C') ¶ An owned Eigen sparse vector or matrix. Parameters: data: A shape (integer or tuple), dense data, sparse array, or SciPy sparse object. dtype: Signed integer, float32/64, or complex64/128 dtype. Inferred from data. order: "C" for row-major or "F" for column-major storage. Defaults to "C". Tuple input specifies a shape. Use :func: sppy.asarray to treat tuples as data. Sparse indexing returns independent copies, rather than views. dtype property ¶ Stored NumPy scalar dtype. shape property ¶ Logical vector or matrix dimensions. order property ¶ 'C' for row storage, 'F' for column storage. nnz property ¶ Number of stored entries, including explicit zeros. stored_indices() ¶ Coordinates in storage order, aligned with :meth: values , including zeros. nonzero() ¶ Coordinates of nonzero values, excluding explicitly stored zeros. values() ¶ Return a copy of stored values aligned with :meth: stored_indices . put(data, row_indices, column_indices=None, *, init=False) ¶ Assign paired coordinates; init=True replaces storage and sums duplicates. from_triplets(shape, rows, columns, values, *, dtype=None, order='C') classmethod ¶ Assemble a matrix from unsorted coordinates; duplicate entries are summed. from_compressed(shape, values, indices, indptr, *, order='C', dtype=None) classmethod ¶ Copy CSR (C) or CSC (F) arrays, validating pointer bounds and indices. compressed_arrays() ¶ Return independent (values, indices, indptr) copies in CSR/CSC order. toarray() ¶ Allocate a dense array, preserving dtype. to_scipy_csr() ¶ Copy into a SciPy CSR matrix (SciPy is optional). to_scipy_csc() ¶ Copy into a SciPy CSC matrix (SciPy is optional). copy(order='K') ¶ Independent copy, optionally changing storage order. astype(dtype, order='K', casting='unsafe', subok=True, copy=True) ¶ Cast stored values without allocating a dense array. multiply(other) ¶ Elementwise sparse multiplication, with matching shapes. dot(other) ¶ Matrix/vector product, equivalent to @ (without conjugation). parallel_dot(other) ¶ Dense product using Eigen's configured thread count and optional OpenMP. transpose(*axes) ¶ Return a sparse copy with axes reversed. conjugate() ¶ Conjugate stored values without changing sparsity. adjoint() ¶ Conjugate transpose (H). reserve(n) ¶ Reserve a total capacity, or additional capacity per outer vector. compress() ¶ Convert to compressed storage. uncompress() ¶ Enable uncompressed insertion storage. squeeze() ¶ Compress storage and release unused entry capacity. set_zero() ¶ Remove all entries while preserving shape. fill(value) ¶ Fill every position; nonzero values store the entire logical array. ones() ¶ Fill every position with one. resize(shape, *, preserve=False) ¶ Resize in place; preserve=True retains entries within new bounds. prune(tolerance=1e-12) ¶ Remove entries whose absolute value is at most tolerance, in place. eliminate_zeros() ¶ Remove only exact stored zeros, in place. triangular(*, lower=True, unit_diagonal=False) ¶ Materialize a sparse lower/upper triangular copy. selfadjoint(*, lower=True) ¶ Reconstruct a Hermitian matrix from its lower or upper triangle. permuted(rows=None, columns=None) ¶ Gather rows/columns in permutation order; vectors accept only rows. row_indices(row) ¶ Stored column indices in a row. column_indices(column) ¶ Stored row indices in a column. submatrix(start_row, start_column, rows, columns) ¶ Copy a rectangular block. vdot(other) ¶ Conjugating inner product of equally sized sparse vectors. outer(other) ¶ Sparse vector outer product without conjugation. lp_norm(p=2) ¶ Entrywise p-norm for p >= 1, including the infinity norm. normalize() ¶ Normalize a floating-point or complex vector in place. set_identity() ¶ Replace a matrix with an identity of the same (possibly rectangular) shape. set_diagonal(values, offset=0) ¶ Assign a diagonal without allocating the full matrix. swap(other) ¶ Exchange owned storage in constant time; dtype/order/dimensionality must match. insert_from_triplets(rows, columns, values) ¶ Add triplets to existing entries, summing duplicate contributions. scale_rows(values) ¶ Return diag(values) @ self without forming the diagonal matrix. scale_columns(values) ¶ Return self @ diag(values) without forming the diagonal matrix. unary(function) ¶ Map a NumPy-compatible function, including implicit zeros. If function(0) is nonzero, every logical position must be stored. abs2() ¶ Squared magnitudes, with real output for complex input. minimum(other) ¶ Elementwise minimum, including implicit zeros. maximum(other) ¶ Elementwise maximum, including implicit zeros. squared_norm() ¶ Squared Euclidean/Frobenius norm, accumulated in floating point. normalized() ¶ Return a vector divided by its Euclidean norm; zero vectors remain zero. is_approx(other, *, rtol=1e-05, atol=1e-08) ¶ Compare equal-shaped arrays using a Frobenius error bound, without densifying. is_zero(tolerance=0) ¶ Whether all stored values are within an absolute tolerance of zero. ceil() ¶ Apply numpy.ceil elementwise, including implicit zeros. clip(min=None, max=None, out=None, **kwargs) ¶ Clamp values to bounds as NumPy does, including implicit zeros. cos() ¶ Apply numpy.cos elementwise, including implicit zeros. floor() ¶ Apply numpy.floor elementwise, including implicit zeros. max(axis=None, out=None, keepdims=False) ¶ Maximum including implicit zeros; empty arrays return NaN. mean(axis=None, dtype=None, out=None, keepdims=False) ¶ Compute means without materializing implicit zeros. min(axis=None, out=None, keepdims=False) ¶ Minimum including implicit zeros; empty arrays return NaN. power(exponent) ¶ Elementwise power; equivalent to self ** exponent . sign() ¶ Apply numpy.sign elementwise, including implicit zeros. sin() ¶ Apply numpy.sin elementwise, including implicit zeros. std(axis=None, dtype=None, out=None, ddof=0, keepdims=False) ¶ Standard deviation with NumPy-compatible reduction arguments. sum(axis=None, dtype=None, out=None, keepdims=False) ¶ Sum values, including NumPy's axis/dtype/out/keepdims conventions. trace(offset=0, axis1=0, axis2=1, dtype=None, out=None) ¶ Sum a diagonal, with NumPy's trace arguments. var(axis=None, dtype=None, out=None, ddof=0, keepdims=False) ¶ Variance including implicit zeros, using a stable centered sum. diagonal(offset=0, axis1=0, axis2=1) ¶ Extract a diagonal as a dense vector, without densifying the matrix. subarray(row_indices, column_indices=None) ¶ Take the Cartesian product of index vectors, like NumPy's ix_. count_nonzero(axis=None) ¶ Count nonzero values, excluding explicitly stored zeros.

docs.text: Eigen sparse coverage ¶ SpPy 1.0 targets the built-in modules shipped with Eigen 5.0.1 . The Python interface materializes owned results instead of exposing C++ expression-template objects. No SciPy dependency is required for the features in this table. Eigen module SpPy interface SparseCore SparseArray , vector/matrix storage in C/F order, indexing and blocks, triplets, CSR/CSC import/export, reserve/compress/uncompress/squeeze, resize/swap, pruning, arithmetic, sparse/dense products, reductions, diagonal scaling, coefficient operations, triangular/Hermitian materialization, adjoint, permutations OrderingMethods linalg.ordering(a, "amd"/"colamd"/"natural") , ordering selection on direct factorizations SparseCholesky SimplicialLLT , SimplicialLDLT , symbolic analysis, numerical refactorization, dense/sparse RHS solves, sparse L/U factors, LDLT D, permutations, determinant, diagonal shifts SparseLU SparseLU , symbolic analysis, numerical refactorization, dense/sparse RHS solves, sparse L/U, row/column permutations, determinant/log determinant, pivot threshold SparseQR SparseQR , rectangular least squares, symbolic analysis, numerical refactorization, rank, sparse R, implicit Q/Q.H application, column permutation, pivot threshold IterativeLinearSolvers cg , bicgstab , lscg , initial guesses, multiple RHS, iteration/error/status diagnostics, identity/diagonal/least-square diagonal/incomplete LU/incomplete Cholesky preconditioners See the array API and solver API for signatures. Precision and ownership ¶ Arrays support signed 8/16/32/64-bit integers, float32/64, and complex64/128. Solvers operate natively in float32/64 or complex64/128; cast integer arrays explicitly before solving. Sparse vectors use an owned single-column Eigen matrix internally, with one outer pointer and NumPy-style one-dimensional behavior in Python. Their native entry storage is proportional to stored entries, even for large logical vector sizes. Dimensions and storage indices are signed 32-bit integers. Each matrix has one storage order; arithmetic converts compatible inputs when needed. Compressed arrays and factors are copies. Changing them cannot invalidate an Eigen object. Deliberate boundaries ¶ This is a Python interface to the built-in modules, not a binding of every C++ template overload. Non-owning Eigen::Map / Ref , raw pointer mutation, expression lifetimes, custom C++ scalar types, custom C++ ordering functors, and custom C++ preconditioner classes are not exposed. Boolean and unsigned storage, 64-bit storage indices, are not supported. LDLT is intended for positive definite systems, rather than a general pivoted symmetric-indefinite solver. External support modules (SuiteSparse, SuperLU, MKL/Pardiso, PaStiX, METIS, Accelerate) and Eigen's unsupported modules are outside this release's scope. Newer Eigen APIs beyond the 5.0.1 baseline are not implied by these bindings. For the upstream module overview, see Eigen's sparse tutorial and built-in sparse solvers .

docs.text: Installation ¶ SpPy requires Python 3.11 or newer, Eigen 5.0.1 or newer, and a C++17 compiler. The native build uses scikit-build-core and CMake, with pybind11 3 installed automatically in an isolated build environment. CMake and Ninja are provisioned by the backend when suitable tools are not installed. Install uv using https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/. Download and extract Eigen from https://libeigen.gitlab.io/ separately. Creating the development environment ¶ From a source checkout on Linux or macOS: export EIGEN_INCLUDE_DIR=/path/to/eigen-5.0.1 uv sync --locked uv run --locked pytest uv sync creates .venv and installs the project in editable mode, along with the default dev dependency group. No activation is needed for uv run . The committed uv.lock records the resolved dependency versions; .python-version selects Python 3.14. Override the interpreter with, for example, uv sync --locked --python 3.12 . The Eigen include directory must contain Eigen/Core . Installed Eigen CMake packages, standard system include directories, and vendor/eigen are searched when EIGEN_INCLUDE_DIR is unset. On Windows, set the variable in PowerShell: $env:EIGEN_INCLUDE_DIR = "C:\path\to\eigen-5.0.1" uv sync --locked uv run --locked pytest Use an MSVC developer shell with C++17 support. Linux is validated locally; macOS and Windows have not been validated locally. Minimal environments and SciPy ¶ To omit development dependencies: uv sync --locked --no-dev uv run --locked --no-dev python -c "import sppy; print(sppy.__version__)" For SciPy interoperability and Matrix Market IO, add --extra scipy to sync and run commands. The default development group already includes SciPy. Install with pip ¶ uv is a development convenience, not a runtime dependency. From a source checkout with Eigen configured, a regular installation is supported: python -m pip install . python -m pip install '.[scipy]' The second command also installs SciPy. Source installations need the same compiler and Eigen headers as development builds. Troubleshooting ¶ Eigen not found: point EIGEN_INCLUDE_DIR at the directory containing Eigen/Core , rather than the Eigen subdirectory itself. Use Eigen 5.0.1+. Compiler errors: check that a C++17 compiler is available. On Windows, use an MSVC developer shell. SciPy import errors: add --extra scipy to both uv sync and uv run when using --no-dev . Stale native build: run uv sync --locked --reinstall-package sppy after updating external Eigen headers. For checks, OpenMP builds, release artifacts, and documentation previews, see contributing .

docs.text: NumPy and SciPy interoperability ¶ NumPy ¶ SpPy follows common NumPy naming and indexing conventions, but does not implement the complete array-function or ufunc dispatch protocols. Prefer methods such as a.sum(axis=0) and operators such as a @ b to keep the conversion boundary explicit. import numpy as np import sppy a = sppy.asarray([[0, 2], [3, 0]], dtype=np.int64) dense = np.asarray(a) assert dense.dtype == np.int64 assert a.sum() == 5 Dense conversion preserves the stored dtype, including exact int64 values. np.asarray(a) always allocates dense storage. Other NumPy functions may also coerce to dense arrays; do not assume they preserve sparsity. Supported storage dtypes are signed 8/16/32/64-bit integers and 32/64-bit floats. Complex64/128 storage is supported. Boolean and unsigned storage are unsupported. Arrays have one or two dimensions. Individual dimensions and stored-entry indices use signed 32-bit limits. General arithmetic broadcasting, whole-array boolean masks, new-axis indexing, and the full set of NumPy reduction keywords are unsupported. SciPy sparse arrays and matrices ¶ Install the scipy extra as described in installation . The default development environment already includes SciPy. from scipy import sparse import sppy source = sparse.csr_array([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]]) a = sppy.asarray(source) csr = a.to_scipy_csr() csc = a.to_scipy_csc() Use the constructor or asarray for conversion into SpPy. There is no fromScipySparse method. Conversion allocates new storage. Matrix Market files ¶ from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory from pathlib import Path import sppy from sppy.io import mmread, mmwrite with TemporaryDirectory() as directory: path = Path(directory) / "matrix.mtx" mmwrite(path, sppy.eye(3), comment="Example identity matrix") restored = mmread(path) assert restored.shape == (3, 3) Matrix Market IO requires two-dimensional arrays and SciPy. The reader supports comments, symmetry, and compressed input through SciPy. Integer files are loaded as int64 , real files as float64 ; complex files as complex128 . See the IO reference for arguments and storage selection.

docs.text: Linear algebra ¶ These functions call Eigen directly and require no SciPy installation. Solvers accept float32/64 and complex64/128 matrices. Integer matrices must be explicitly cast before solving. See Eigen coverage for the module map. Direct solves and factor reuse ¶ import numpy as np import sppy from sppy.linalg import SparseLU, SparseQR, SimplicialLLT, cg, ComputationInfo a = sppy.asarray([[4., 1.], [1., 3.]]) b = np.array([1., 2.]) factor = SparseLU(a) x = factor.solve(b) np.testing.assert_allclose(a @ x, b) # Reuse the symbolic pattern when only coefficients change. factor.factorize(a * 2) np.testing.assert_allclose((a * 2) @ factor.solve(b), b) Choose LLT/LDLT for Hermitian positive definite systems, LU for general square systems, and QR for rectangular least squares. All support dense vector or matrix right-hand sides and sparse RHS matrices. Sparse RHS solves return SparseArray. Cholesky reads the lower triangle by default; lower=False uses the upper triangle. Its shift_offset and shift_scale transform the diagonal as scale * diagonal + offset . Direct factorization failures raise numpy.linalg.LinAlgError . Analyze and factorize are separate operations; compute performs both. Numeric refactorization requires an identical stored sparsity pattern, including explicitly stored zeros. Changing the matrix afterward does not alter an existing factorization. Factors and implicit Q ¶ Cholesky exposes factor("L") , factor("U") , and factor("P") ; LDLT also exposes factor("D") . LU exposes sparse L / U , row P and column Q permutations, a determinant, and a stable slogdet() . QR exposes sparse R , column P , numerical rank , and apply_q(rhs, adjoint=False) without allocating a full dense Q. Permutation arrays follow Eigen's convention: P[indices[j], j] = 1 . The empty Cholesky permutation represents identity when no reordering is needed. rectangular = sppy.asarray([[1., 0.], [0., 1.], [1., 1.]]) qr = SparseQR(rectangular) least_squares = qr.solve(np.array([1., 2., 3.])) assert qr.rank == 2 np.testing.assert_allclose(rectangular @ least_squares, [1., 2., 3.]) Iterative solves ¶ result = cg(a, b, preconditioner="incomplete_cholesky", rtol=1e-10) assert result.info == ComputationInfo.SUCCESS np.testing.assert_allclose(a @ result.solution, b) x, status = result Function Matrix Available preconditioners cg Hermitian positive definite; both triangles are read identity, diagonal (default), incomplete_cholesky bicgstab General square identity, diagonal (default), incomplete_lut lscg Rectangular least squares identity, least_square_diagonal (default) Options include x0 , rtol , and maxiter . ILUT adds drop_tolerance and fill_factor ; incomplete Cholesky adds initial_shift . Results expose solution , info , iterations , and estimated relative error . For multiple RHS columns, diagnostics report the worst column. LSCG's error is measured on the normal equations. Inspect info before using a nonconverged result. Preconditioner(a, method=...) builds an independently reusable inverse preconditioner with a .solve(rhs) method. triangular_solve handles lower, upper, and unit-diagonal systems. ordering computes AMD/COLAMD/natural gather permutations; pass them to a.permuted . Norms and randomized SVD ¶ norm(a) computes a Euclidean vector norm or Frobenius matrix norm. Matrix 1/infinity norms are supported. Randomized SVD returns (u, s, v) and reconstructs as (u * s) @ v.conj().T . It uses local random sampling; pass omega to supply projection directions or rng for reproducible sampling. Solver reference ¶ sppy.linalg.solvers ¶ Eigen's built-in sparse direct and iterative solvers. No SciPy dependency is needed. Native solvers preserve float32/64 and complex64/128 precision and return owned arrays and factors. ComputationInfo ¶ Bases: IntEnum Eigen computation status. IterativeResult dataclass ¶ Solution, Eigen status, iteration count, and estimated relative error. Unpacking yields (solution, info). Inspect iterations/error on the object. For multiple right-hand sides, status, iterations, and error are the worst values across columns. Check info before using a nonconverged solution. SparseFactorization ¶ Reusable Eigen factorization, with separate symbolic and numeric steps. Parameters: a: Optional matrix to factor immediately. method: One of llt, ldlt, lu, or qr. ordering: natural, amd, or colamd. Defaults to amd for Cholesky, colamd for LU/QR. docs.text: import numpy as np import sppy from sppy.linalg import SparseLU, SparseQR, SimplicialLLT, cg, ComputationInfo a = sppy.asarray([[4., 1.], [1., 3.]]) b = np.array([1., 2.]) factor = SparseLU(a) x = factor.solve(b) np.testing.assert_allclose(a @ x, b) # Reuse the symbolic pattern when only coefficients change. factor.factorize(a * 2) np.testing.assert_allclose((a * 2) @ factor.solve(b), b) Choose LLT/LDLT for Hermitian positive definite systems, LU for general square systems, and QR for rectangular least squares. docs.text: Migrating to 1.0 ¶ Version 1.0 is a breaking release. The generated Cython backends have been replaced by a typed pybind11/Eigen implementation, including native complex storage, direct factorizations, iterative solvers, preconditioners, and orderings. Rebuild the package after pulling these changes; old binary extensions are not compatible with the new interface. uv sync --locked --reinstall-package sppy Removed compatibility APIs ¶ Removed Use in 1.0 sppy.csarray , sppy.csarray module sppy.SparseArray , sppy.sparse_array module storagetype , storage_type , storageType order="C" for rows, order="F" for columns toScipyCsr , toScipyCsc to_scipy_csr , to_scipy_csc rowInds , colInds row_indices , column_indices subArray subarray nonzeroRowsList , nonzeroRowsPtr nonzero_rows_list , nonzero_rows_ptr pdot , hadamard , getnnz , diag method parallel_dot , multiply , nnz , diagonal biCGSTAB(maxIter=..., tol=...) bicgstab(maxiter=..., rtol=...) asLinearOperator , asLinearOperatorSum as_linear_operator , as_linear_operator_sum sppy.linalg.GeneralLinearOperator module Import the class from sppy.linalg eye(n, dtype) positional shorthand eye(n, dtype=dtype) prune(eps, precision) prune(tolerance=...) , using an absolute magnitude threshold sppy.lib.Parameter , sppy.lib.Util Ordinary Python/NumPy validation and operations All factories and the direct constructor now default to C order . mmread takes keyword-only order="C" , replacing storagetype . Tuple constructor input still denotes a shape; asarray treats a tuple as data. Old pickle state dictionaries are not supported; export arrays before upgrading. Stored entries versus nonzero values ¶ nnz counts stored entries, including explicit zeros. nonzero() now excludes stored zeros. Code that pairs coordinates with values() must use stored_indices() instead: import sppy a = sppy.eye(3) rows, columns = a.stored_indices() values = a.values() assert len(values) == len(rows) == len(columns) == a.nnz compressed_arrays() returns (values, indices, indptr) in the selected CSR/CSC storage order. Each array is an independent copy. Solvers and complex values ¶ The iterative functions return IterativeResult . Existing tuple unpacking x, status = bicgstab(a, b) still works. The result also exposes iterations and error . Status values use ComputationInfo : success=0, numerical issue=1, no convergence=2, invalid input=3. These are Eigen's values, not SciPy's codes. Use reusable SparseLU , SparseQR , SimplicialLLT , or SimplicialLDLT factors for repeated solves. Direct numerical failures raise numpy.linalg.LinAlgError . Pattern reuse requires the same shape, dtype, and stored coordinates. An unsuccessful refactorization invalidates solving. T is a transpose; H is a conjugate transpose. Linear operators now use the adjoint for reverse products. Randomized SVD reconstructs complex inputs as (u * s) @ v.conj().T ; it uses a local generator instead of global RNG state. rand also uses a local generator; pass rng= to reproduce a workload. NumPy compatibility remains partial: slicing returns copies, arithmetic requires matching shapes, and NumPy coercion can allocate a dense array. See interoperability and the explicit Eigen coverage boundaries .

docs.text: Quick start ¶ After installing SpPy , run these examples in Python. Create an array ¶ Use asarray to convert data and zeros to create an empty sparse array. The conversion infers the dtype; pass dtype explicitly when needed. import numpy as np import sppy a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2., 0.], [3., 0., 4.]]) assert a.shape == (2, 3) assert a.ndim == 2 assert a.size == 6 assert a.nnz == 3 b = sppy.zeros((2, 3), dtype=np.float64) b[0, 1] = 2. b[1, [0, 2]] = [3., 4.] np.testing.assert_array_equal(a.toarray(), b.toarray()) size counts all positions, while nnz counts stored entries. Explicitly stored zeros can contribute to nnz ; use count_nonzero() to count nonzero values. Select and update values ¶ row = a[0] # Sparse vector with shape (3,) column = a[:, 1] # Sparse vector with shape (2,) block = a[:, 1:] # Sparse matrix with shape (2, 2) a[-1, 0] = 5. assert a[1, 0] == 5. Slices are independent copies. Assign through a[...] to change the original. Compute with sparse arrays ¶ squared = a * a product = a @ a.T vector_product = a @ np.ones(3) row_totals = a.sum(axis=1) means = a.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True) assert product.shape == (2, 2) np.testing.assert_array_equal(vector_product, [2., 9.]) np.testing.assert_array_equal(row_totals, [2., 9.]) * multiplies elementwise; @ performs matrix multiplication. Reductions and products with dense vectors return dense results. For larger workloads, read the sparse array guide before converting to dense arrays.

docs.text: Sparse arrays ¶ Construction, dtypes, and storage ¶ import numpy as np import sppy empty = sppy.zeros((5, 7), dtype=np.float32) vector = sppy.zeros(5, dtype=np.int64) identity = sppy.eye(5) diagonal = sppy.diag(np.array([1., 2., 3.])) random = sppy.rand((5, 7), 0.1, rng=np.random.default_rng(21)) columns = sppy.asarray([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]], order="F") Use asarray for data, including tuples. In SparseArray((5, 7)) , the tuple specifies a shape instead of values. asarray infers the input dtype. zeros , ones , and eye default to row storage ( order="C" ). The direct SparseArray constructor and rand also default to row storage. Choose order="F" for column storage and order="C" for row storage. rand samples coordinates with replacement, so the resulting density may be lower than requested. Pass a NumPy Generator for reproducible inputs. Integer dtypes cast the random values, which can produce stored zeros. ones stores every element explicitly. asarray(a) may reuse a compatible sparse array. Request copy=True for an independent object; copy=False raises if conversion requires allocation. Dense inputs always require a copy into Eigen storage. a.copy() and a.astype(np.float32) provide explicit copying and dtype conversion. Indexing and assignment ¶ Integer indices drop an axis; slices preserve it. Negative indices, reversed or stepped slices, per-axis boolean masks, and paired array indices are supported. A slice is a copy, including a basic slice. a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2., 0.], [3., 0., 4.]]) row = a[0] # Shape (3,) rows = a[:1] # Shape (1, 3) reversed_rows = a[::-1] masked = a[np.array([True, False]), :] paired = a[[0, 1], [1, 2]] # Select (0, 1) and (1, 2) cartesian = a.subarray([0, 1], [1, 2]) # Select a 2 by 2 submatrix a[[0, 1], [0, 1]] = [5., 6.] a[:, 2] = 1. Paired indices select coordinate pairs; subarray selects the Cartesian product of row and column indices. Whole-array boolean masks and None (new-axis) indexing are unsupported. Assemble a matrix ¶ Reserve space when the approximate entry count is known, insert entries, then compress to release spare buffer capacity. a = sppy.zeros((1000, 1000)) a.reserve(3) a[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]] = [0.1, 0.2, 0.4] a.compress() Arithmetic and reductions ¶ Expression Operation Result a + b , a - b Same-shape sparse arithmetic Sparse array a * b , a.multiply(b) Same-shape elementwise product Sparse array a * 2 , -a , abs(a) Scalar multiplication, negation, absolute value Sparse array a @ b , a.dot(b) Matrix product of sparse matrices Sparse array a @ dense_vector Matrix-vector product Dense array a.T Transpose Sparse array a.sum(axis=0) Column sums Dense array a.diagonal() Main diagonal Dense array A sparse vector dotted with another sparse vector returns a scalar. Sparse arithmetic promotes dtypes. General arithmetic broadcasting is unsupported, and nonzero scalar addition raises NotImplementedError . sum , mean , min , max , var , and std accept axis , out , and keepdims . Sum, mean, variance, and standard deviation also accept dtype ; variance and standard deviation accept ddof . Implicit zeros participate in reductions. Empty min/max retain the historical NaN result. Stored zeros and memory ¶ a.nnz counts stored entries, including stored zeros. a.count_nonzero() counts nonzero values. a.eliminate_zeros() removes exact zeros in place; a.prune(tolerance=...) removes entries using an absolute magnitude threshold. Operations that can fill an array a.toarray() and np.asarray(a) allocate dense storage. ones , cos , clipping to a positive lower bound, and other operations that map zero to a nonzero value can store every position. Estimate the full array size before applying these operations to large shapes. Prefer sparse methods when memory matters. NumPy interoperability explains the conversion boundaries, and the API reference lists the available methods. Eigen storage and structured operations ¶ Assemble unsorted entries with SparseArray.from_triplets(shape, rows, columns, values) . Duplicate contributions are summed. insert_from_triplets adds contributions to existing entries. Import CSR/CSC arrays with from_compressed and export independent (values, indices, indptr) copies with compressed_arrays . is_compressed , inner_size , and outer_size describe the native layout. reserve accepts total capacity or a vector of capacities per outer row/column. uncompress enables insertion storage; compress restores compressed storage; squeeze also frees unused entry capacity. resize(shape, preserve=True) retains in-bounds entries; the default discards data. swap exchanges matching storage objects in constant time. triangular(lower=..., unit_diagonal=...) materializes a triangle. selfadjoint(lower=...) reconstructs a Hermitian matrix from one triangle. T transposes and H conjugate-transposes. real , imag , conjugate , and abs2 support complex coefficients. scale_rows / scale_columns multiply by diagonal scales without forming a diagonal matrix. Use stored_indices() when pairing coordinates with values() ; nonzero() excludes explicitly stored zeros. minimum / maximum compare sparse arrays including implicit zeros. unary(function) applies a NumPy-compatible function to all values, including implicit zeros. A nonzero result at zero fills every position, as with exp or log . Scalar / and in-place arithmetic ( += , -= , *= , /= ) are supported. In-place arithmetic keeps object identity and rejects dtype changes that cannot be cast with NumPy's same-kind rule. vdot conjugates the first sparse vector; dot and outer do not. lp_norm computes an entrywise norm and normalize normalizes a floating-point or complex vector in place. Basic integer/slice selections run in native sparse code without allocating full-axis index grids. Same-dtype copies and storage-order changes use direct native storage operations. Canonical compressed buffers are validated and copied directly; unsorted or duplicate compressed entries use the summing assembly path. Copies retain the source compression state when storage order is unchanged.

docs.text: import numpy as np import sppy empty = sppy.zeros((5, 7), dtype=np.float32) vector = sppy.zeros(5, dtype=np.int64) identity = sppy.eye(5) diagonal = sppy.diag(np.array([1., 2., 3.])) random = sppy.rand((5, 7), 0.1, rng=np.random.default_rng(21)) columns = sppy.asarray([[0., 2.], [3., 0.]], order="F") Use asarray for data, including tuples. In SparseArray((5, 7)) , the tuple specifies a shape instead of values. asarray infers the input dtype. zeros , ones , and eye default to row storage ( order="C" ). The direct SparseArray constructor and rand also default to row storage. Choose order="F" for column storage and order="C" for row storage. rand samples coordinates with replacement, so the resulting density may be lower than requested. Pass a NumPy Generator for reproducible inputs. Integer dtypes cast the random values, which can produce stored zeros. ones stores every element explicitly. asarray(a) may reuse a compatible sparse array. Request copy=True for an independent object; copy=False raises if conversion requires allocation. Dense inputs always require a copy into Eigen storage. a.copy() and a.astype(np.float32) provide explicit copying and dtype conversion.

docs.text: Integer indices drop an axis; slices preserve it. Negative indices, reversed or stepped slices, per-axis boolean masks, and paired array indices are supported. A slice is a copy, including a basic slice. a = sppy.asarray([[0., 2., 0.], [3., 0., 4.]]) row = a[0] # Shape (3,) rows = a[:1] # Shape (1, 3) reversed_rows = a[::-1] masked = a[np.array([True, False]), :] paired = a[[0, 1], [1, 2]] # Select (0, 1) and (1, 2) cartesian = a.subarray([0, 1], [1, 2]) # Select a 2 by 2 submatrix a[[0, 1], [0, 1]] = [5., 6.] a[:, 2] = 1. Paired indices select coordinate pairs; subarray selects the Cartesian product of row and column indices. Whole-array boolean masks and None (new-axis) indexing are unsupported.

General arithmetic broadcasting is unsupported, and nonzero scalar addition raises NotImplementedError . sum , mean , min , max , var , and std accept axis , out , and keepdims . docs.text: a.nnz counts stored entries, including stored zeros. a.count_nonzero() counts nonzero values. a.eliminate_zeros() removes exact zeros in place; a.prune(tolerance=...) removes entries using an absolute magnitude threshold. Operations that can fill an array a.toarray() and np.asarray(a) allocate dense storage. ones , cos , clipping to a positive lower bound, and other operations that map zero to a nonzero value can store every position. Estimate the full array size before applying these operations to large shapes. Prefer sparse methods when memory matters. NumPy interoperability explains the conversion boundaries, and the API reference lists the available methods.

docs.text: Assemble unsorted entries with SparseArray.from_triplets(shape, rows, columns, values) . Duplicate contributions are summed. insert_from_triplets adds contributions to existing entries. Import CSR/CSC arrays with from_compressed and export independent (values, indices, indptr) copies with compressed_arrays . is_compressed , inner_size , and outer_size describe the native layout. reserve accepts total capacity or a vector of capacities per outer row/column. uncompress enables insertion storage; compress restores compressed storage; squeeze also frees unused entry capacity. resize(shape, preserve=True) retains in-bounds entries; the default discards data. swap exchanges matching storage objects in constant time. triangular(lower=..., unit_diagonal=...) materializes a triangle. selfadjoint(lower=...) reconstructs a Hermitian matrix from one triangle. T transposes and H conjugate-transposes. real , imag , conjugate , and abs2 support complex coefficients. scale_rows / scale_columns multiply by diagonal scales without forming a diagonal matrix. Use stored_indices() when pairing coordinates with values() ; nonzero() excludes explicitly stored zeros. minimum / maximum compare sparse arrays including implicit zeros. unary(function) applies a NumPy-compatible function to all values, including implicit zeros. A nonzero result at zero fills every position, as with exp or log . Scalar / and in-place arithmetic ( += , -= , *= , /= ) are supported. In-place arithmetic keeps object identity and rejects dtype changes that cannot be cast with NumPy's same-kind rule. vdot conjugates the first sparse vector; dot and outer do not. lp_norm computes an entrywise norm and normalize normalizes a floating-point or complex vector in place. Basic integer/slice selections run in native sparse code without allocating full-axis index grids. Same-dtype copies and storage-order changes use direct native storage operations. Canonical compressed buffers are validated and copied directly; unsorted or duplicate compressed entries use the summing assembly path. Copies retain the source compression state when storage order is unchanged.
